question: How is the final overall grade calculated?
expected_answer: Weighted mean of module grades plus the thesis grade, weighted by ECTS; only the first decimal place counts and further digits are dropped without rounding (§ 25 Abs. 2)
actual_answer: ANSWER  The final overall grade (*Gesamtnote*) is calculated as the weighted average of the module grades of compulsory and elective modules, as well as the grade of the Master's thesis and, if applicable, the oral Master's examination and/or thesis defense [D1 § 25 Abs. 2 Sätze 1–7].   The weight of a module grade is determined by the sum of the weights of its component sub-modules, and the weight of the Master's thesis/oral exam is generally given by its assigned ECTS credits [D1 § 25 Abs. 2 Sätze 1–7].   When calculating the overall grade, only the first decimal place after the comma is considered, and all subsequent decimal places are truncated without rounding [D1 § 25 Abs. 2 Sätze 1–7].   The overall grade corresponds to the following grade bands [D1 § 25 Abs. 2 Sätze 1–7]: - Up to 1.5: Very good (*sehr gut*) - 1.6 to 2.5: Good (*gut*) - 2.6 to 3.5: Satisfactory (*befriedigend*) - 3.6 to 4.0: Sufficient (*ausreichend*) - 4.1 and above: Insufficient (*nicht ausreichend*)
